title: Sign in with ChatGPT — contract — acceptance

steps.surface: Settings → Model Providers · First-run screen · Chat view · Status bar · Model picker
steps.path: Settings → Model Providers → ChatGPT; First run → sign in; conversation on a ChatGPT model
steps.headline: The contract, graded — accept these verdicts?

rows.statement: The ChatGPT sign-in lives in two places: a ChatGPT card in Settings → Model Providers and a second button on the first-run screen.
The provider is called ChatGPT on its Settings card, and its models are listed by their own names, such as GPT-5.6.
Every model the signed-in plan allows appears in the model picker, grouped together, and a new model appears when OpenAI ships it.
The /usage card and the status-bar chips show both the 5-hour and 7-day windows of the ChatGPT plan, with reset times.
When the plan runs out mid-conversation, the turn stops with a card naming the reset time and a way to switch provider.
The ChatGPT card's (i) note says the plan is used through OpenAI's own sign-in, allowed today but not promised in writing.
A ChatGPT card sits between Claude Code and OpenRouter in Model Providers, with a Sign in button instead of a key box.
rows.note: fine but we should no longer show "Default engine" on the claude code tab. al providers should be formatted similarly with neutral treatment
rows.evidence: I opened Settings → Model Providers in the running workbench and read the whole panel back: the three cloud cards come out in the order Claude Code, ChatGPT, OpenRouter, and the ChatGPT card carries a "Sign in with ChatGPT" button with no key box anywhere on it. Your note is done too — there is no "Default engine" badge or green connected text left, and all three cards use the one neutral card shape (name, one grey status line, one button on the right).

rows.statement: The signed-in line matches the app's other status text, and the Claude Code card shows plan usage whenever the ChatGPT card does.
rows.note: i don't like the signed in text. it doesn't really match any styling use'd elsewhere in the app. figure out how to make this more consistent with other surfaces. and add usage to the cc card if doing that for gpt.

rows.statement: In a conversation on a ChatGPT model the status bar shows the plan's 5h and 7d chips, each with its reset time.
rows.evidence: In a live conversation on a ChatGPT model the status bar showed exactly two chips, "5h: 34% Resets @ 8:45am" and "7d: 12% Resets Thursday @ 6:35am", both pointing at the ChatGPT plan rather than claude.ai. Amended per W-2, which you approved: a Plus or Pro plan still shows exactly 5h and 7d, but your own free account reports one 30-day window, so it shows a single "30d" chip — a test pins that output too. The chip and the limit card now spell the day the same way (you chose the full "Tuesday" on 2026-09-05), and a test holds them together.

rows.statement: Typing /usage in a ChatGPT conversation shows the plan's two windows and says they are measured across the whole ChatGPT plan.
rows.evidence: The test that pins the /usage card's exact markup for a ChatGPT session passes: it draws the 5-hour and 7-day bars with their reset times and ends with the line "Measured across your whole ChatGPT plan, not just this conversation." Amended per W-2, which you approved: on a plan whose windows are a different length — your free account's single 30-day one — the card draws one "30-day limit" row instead, with the same ChatGPT-plan sentence under it.

rows.statement: The plan's models appear in the model picker labelled the way OpenAI names them, each marked with its provider.
rows.evidence: I opened the model picker in the running workbench and searched "gpt": the plan's models list as "GPT-5.6 Sol · ChatGPT Plan", "GPT-5.6 Terra · ChatGPT Plan", "GPT-5.6 Luna · ChatGPT Plan" and "GPT-5.5 · ChatGPT Plan", each with the green OpenAI mark. The names are not written into the app — the code takes OpenAI's own display name off the account's model list and drops the rows OpenAI marks hidden, which the recorded real-account list confirms.

rows.statement: While the browser tab is open, the ChatGPT card shows one short waiting line with a spinner and a Cancel, nothing else.
rows.evidence: I put the running card into its waiting state and read it back: the whole card is "ChatGPT", a spinner, "Waiting for the browser…", and a Cancel button — nothing else, no extra sentence and no usage bars.

rows.statement: When OpenAI refuses the account, the status stays grey and OpenAI's own reason sits on a red line beneath it, with Sign out.
rows.evidence: I put the running card into its refused state and read it back: the status line stays the ordinary grey "Signed in as destin@example.com", OpenAI's own reason ("Your workspace admin has turned off Codex for this account.") sits on its own line in the red warning colour beneath it, and the button is Sign out. The code takes that sentence verbatim from OpenAI's reply rather than composing a guess.

rows.statement: The first-run card stacks three full-width sign-ins, Claude filled, ChatGPT and OpenRouter outlined, and its link reads Use an API key or local model.
rows.evidence: I loaded the first-run sign-in screen in the running workbench: it shows three stacked full-width buttons — Log in with Claude, Log in with ChatGPT, Log in with OpenRouter — with a link underneath reading "Use an API key or local model". In the code the Claude button is the filled one and the other two are the outlined variant, as approved.

rows.statement: While the browser is open the first-run card stays, holding the waiting line, and the Skip setup link is gone from every step.
rows.evidence: I loaded the first-run screen mid-sign-in: the same bordered card stays in place and holds one line — a spinner plus "A browser window should have opened. Finish signing in to ChatGPT there…" — with no buttons and no link under it. Searching the whole app for the old "Skip setup" link returns only a comment saying it was removed, so it is gone from every step.

rows.statement: In the model picker and the status-bar chip the plan's models are grouped under ChatGPT Plan; the Settings card stays ChatGPT.
rows.evidence: In the running app the picker rows read "· ChatGPT Plan", the picker's provider filter chip says "ChatGPT Plan", and the popup the status-bar model chip opens reads "GPT-5.6 Sol · ChatGPT Plan", while the Settings card title is still the plain word "ChatGPT" — all four checked by reading the live screens. Worth knowing: the status-bar chip itself shows only the model name and the OpenAI mark ("GPT 5.6 Sol"), never a provider name — that is how it has always behaved for every provider, and the "ChatGPT Plan" label appears the moment you click it.

rows.statement: The Claude Code and ChatGPT headings above the cards are gone; each card carries its (i) beside its name.
rows.note: still need to remove the duplicative openrouter/api header, as we did for claude code/chatgpt. we will add two new topline headers (Cloud Models, Local Models) and remove the others. reduce the spacing a tad between the claude code/chatgpt cards
rows.evidence: Reading the live Model Providers panel back, the only headings left are the two group ones, Cloud Models and Local Models — the old "Claude Code" and "ChatGPT" labels above the cards are gone. Each of the three cards carries its own (i) beside its name: About Claude Code, About ChatGPT sign-in, About OpenRouter.

rows.statement: Every provider card's button is pinned to the top right on the name's line, however many lines the status takes.
rows.evidence: I measured the three live cards on screen: on all of them the button's top edge is within five pixels of the card name's, and each sits the same twelve pixels from the card's right edge — including the tallest card, whose status runs to several lines plus two usage bars, and the shortest one-line card.

rows.statement: The used-up card reads You have reached ChatGPT's 5-hour session limit (Resets @ 6:43pm), and Switch Providers opens the model picker.
rows.evidence: I made the running app hit the plan limit and read the card back: it says exactly "You have reached ChatGPT's 5-hour session limit (Resets @ 6:43pm)." with a single Switch Providers button and no Try again, and clicking that button opened the model picker. The weekly version of the same card now names the day too, which you approved on W-1 — and since 2026-09-05 it spells it out in full ("Resets Tuesday @ 6:43pm") so it reads the same as the 7-day chip beside it, which is unchanged.

rows.statement: Model Providers has two group headings, Cloud Models and Local Models; the OpenRouter/API heading is gone and the cloud cards sit closer.
rows.note: looks good aside from the stray ollama row. wouldnt that be local?
rows.evidence: Reading the live panel back, it has exactly two group headings — CLOUD MODELS and LOCAL MODELS — the old OpenRouter/API heading is gone, and the three cloud cards sit in one tight stack with the app's smallest gap between them.

rows.statement: A custom endpoint pointing at this computer, like Ollama, lists under Local Models instead of under the OpenRouter card.
rows.evidence: The named guard test passes (both of its cases). It checks that every way of writing "this computer" — localhost, 127.0.0.1, ::1, 0.0.0.0 — counts as local, and that a server elsewhere (a company API, a machine on your home network) does not, so a broadening later cannot quietly drag a remote server under Local Models. In the running app the Ollama endpoint now appears under Local Models, not under the OpenRouter card.
